connections.why: Organelles such as ribosomes and mitochondria carry out the cell's chemistry
Membrane structure governs the diffusion, osmosis and active transport that supply cells
Enzymes catalyse the reactions that release energy in respiration
Glucose made in photosynthesis is the fuel respiration releases as ATP
DNA carries the genes that are passed on through inheritance
As organisms scale up, simple diffusion is too slow so exchange and transport systems are needed
Transport systems deliver the substances homeostasis must keep balanced
Nervous and hormonal systems coordinate responses on different timescales
Hormones such as insulin maintain stable internal conditions
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that flows through every food web
Respiration and decay return carbon to the cycles running through ecosystems
Inherited variation is the raw material natural selection acts on
Selective breeding applies the principles of selection to food production
Monitoring ecosystems reveals threats to biodiversity
Circulatory transport explains how pathogens and drugs spread through the body
Many treatments work by altering hormonal or cellular signalling
